page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz across 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The instance features 32 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a dedicated 150 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 4 Gbps. Acceleration instructions include AVX-512 and VNNI, while dedicated graphics processing units are absent.

Benchmark results place the computational throughput of the r5dn.xlarge primarily in the lower quartiles relative to modern compute profiles. Synthetic CPU tests show a PassMark CPU score of 3,883.71 and Geekbench scores of 1,123.0 single-core and 2,443.0 multi-core, reflecting the constraints of its two physical cores. Memory performance registers an average PassMark memory score of 2,037.78, with uncached read throughput at 26.99 GB/sec and write throughput at 22.99 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 3.41 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 3.43 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage paired with 32 GB of RAM provides cost-efficient operational density for workloads that prioritize low-latency scratch disk access and high memory footprints over raw processor concurrency. The core tradeoffs involve modest multi-threaded processing power and baseline networking in exchange for dedicated local storage and elevated memory capacity per core. This hardware profile aligns with medium in-memory caches, localized relational database instances, distributed cache nodes, and data transformation jobs requiring fast temporary scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive and I/O-sensitive workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 32 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 RAM. The instance integrates 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results reflect moderate compute throughput, with a PassMark CPU score of 3,883.71, Geekbench multi-core score of 2,443.0, and an average memory score of 2,037.78, reaching 3.41 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. The pairing of local low-latency NVMe scratch space and an 8 GB per vCPU allocation makes this configuration cost-efficient for in-memory databases, key-value stores, caching tiers, and temporary data staging tasks requiring swift local read and write operations.
